People told not to enter damaged buildings for fear of aftershocks from magnitude-7.8 quake

Xi Jinping has arrived in North Korea for a two-day trip, his first in nearly seven years, as China’s leader looks to revitalise ties with his junior ally.

Footage published by China’s Xinhua state news agency showed an Air China plane carrying Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, touching down at Pyongyang’s Sunan international airport.

India declares onset as up to 280mm of rain falls in 72 hours in Kerala, while downpours hit south-west Thailand

rfi.title: France moves closer to ocean goals with three new marine protection zones
rfi.description: The French government has announced three new marine protected areas, bringing it a step closer to goals established at the 2025 United Nations Ocean Summit. These "strong protection" zones are situated in mainland France, in the French West Indies and the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.

rfi.title: Merz, Macron agree to halt FCAS fighter jet plan: Berlin
rfi.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron have agreed to abandon a joint fighter jet programme due to long-running disagreements between the companies involved, the German government said Monday.

rfi.title: French NATO jets destroy mystery drone over Latvia as Ukraine war intensifies
rfi.description: French NATO fighter jets stationed in the Baltic region shot down a drone that had entered Latvian airspace on Monday, marking a rare interception under the alliance’s Baltic Air Policing mission. It follows a series of similar incidents linked to the war in Ukraine as Moscow and Kyiv step up drone strikes on each other.

rfi.title: EU says Ebola outbreak makes ceasefire in DRC more necessary than ever
rfi.description: The European Union’s crisis management commissioner has called for a ceasefire between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda, saying the need for peace has become even more urgent with the spread of the Ebola outbreak.

rfi.title: French prosecutors ordered to review all child abuse complaints after girl's murder
rfi.description: French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin has ordered a review of all complaints involving child victims of sexual violence in France after the death of an 11-year-old girl allegedly killed by a man who had previously been accused of rape and sexual assault of other children but had never been convicted.

rfi.title: World Cup venues: Estadio Azteca, Mexico City
rfi.description: Sixteen stadiums in Mexico, Canada and the United States will stage the games during the first 48-team World Cup. RFI looks at the venues to be used between 11 June and 19 July.

rfi.title: Football history: Jules Rimet, the man behind the World Cup plan
rfi.description: Jules Rimet's brainchild has come a long way in 96 years. Fourteen teams accepted an invitation to take part in the inaugural tournament in 1930. In 2026, more than half of the 48 squads competing have battled through two years of qualifying games.

rfi.title: World Cup venues: Guadalajara Stadium, Mexico
rfi.description: Sixteen stadiums in Mexico, Canada and the United States will stage the games during the first 48-team World Cup. RFI looks at the venues to be used between 11 June and 19 July.

rfi.title: Armenia PM Pashinyan wins vote, cementing pro-Western shift
rfi.description: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's ruling party has won parliamentary elections, preliminary results showed on Monday, a victory seen as endorsement of the nation's pro-Western shift after threats from Moscow and claims of Russian interference.

rfi.title: French singer Patrick Bruel held for questioning over sexual assault allegations
rfi.description: The popular French singer and actor Patrick Bruel has been taken into police custody as part of an investigation into alleged rape and sexual assault involving at least 13 women.

rfi.title: Scientists sound alarm on World Oceans Day as Trump axes deep-sea monitoring
rfi.description: The United States has removed hundreds of deep-sea instruments used to monitor the impact of climate change on marine environments, alarming scientists as the United Nations marks World Oceans Day.

rfi.title: France, UK, Germany back face-to-face Ukraine-Russia ceasefire talks
rfi.description: The leaders of France, Britain and Germany said they support a proposal for direct ceasefire talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin, following defence talks in London on Sunday.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Democratic Republic of Congo return renamed
rfi.description: Democratic Republic of Congo enter the first 48-team World Cup as Africa's ninth best side in the Fifa rankings. In the eighth instalment of a nine-part series on African squads at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada, RFI looks at a nation competing for the first time in 50 years.

rfi.title: Zverev outlasts Cobolli to claim French Open title for the first time
rfi.description: Second seed Alexander Zverev won his first Grand Slam tournament on Sunday night at the Roland Garros French Open after a five-set victory over the 10th seed Flavio Cobolli.

rfi.title: Hard-left Mélenchon launches 2027 campaign with broadside against National Rally
rfi.description: Jean-Luc Melenchon launched his presidential campaign on Sunday with a rally in Saint-Denis, a Paris suburb that has become both a stronghold for the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party and a symbol of the “New France” he hopes to champion.

rfi.title: From pew to pitch, Cameroonian priest builds bridges in French banlieue
rfi.description: In Trappes, one of France's most culturally diverse working-class suburbs – known as banlieues – faith leaders are finding unexpected ways to bring communities together. A Cameroonian-born priest not only fills his church each Sunday, he also hosts interfaith football matches.

rfi.title: Bernadette Chirac, France’s formidable former first lady, dies aged 93
rfi.description: Bernadette Chirac, the formidable former first lady of France who spent 12 years at the Élysée Palace beside President Jacques Chirac while forging her own political identity and transforming a children’s hospital charity into a national institution, has died aged 93.

rfi.title: Pope Leo XIV visits Spain as Church seeks a fresh voice in changing Europe
rfi.description: Pope Leo XIV has begun a weeklong visit to Spain, bringing the American pontiff to one of Europe’s historic centres of Christianity at a moment of political tension, social change and renewed curiosity about faith.

euronews.title: Global uncertainty boosts Spain's tourism, bringing it close to 100 million visitors
euronews.description: International tourist arrivals rose by 5.2% in April to 26.5 million in the first four months. The industry now sees topping 100 million visitors as increasingly likely.

euronews.title: Belgium: Thousands protest alleged police violence in Brussels
euronews.description: Large crowds gathered in Brussels on 8 June to condemn what protesters described as excessive police force during recent demonstrations. The dispute is rooted in planned spending cuts affecting French-speaking education in Belgium

euronews.title: New health risks emerge as Europe’s drug market grows more complex, EU agency warns
euronews.description: Europe’s drug market is growing more complex, with potent opioids, stronger cannabis and new substances raising health risks, the EU agency warns.

euronews.title: Cuba: Powerful offshore earthquake shakes Havana, prompting office evacuation
euronews.description: A powerful earthquake struck western Cuba on 8 June, sending people rushing out of buildings in Havana. Witnesses described scenes of confusion as offices were evacuated and workers waited outside for safety checks.

euronews.title: Video shows Trump booed at NBA Finals game in New York
euronews.description: US President Donald Trump was booed by some spectators as he attended Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden in New York. He appeared during the national anthem before the matchup between the Knicks and the Spurs.

euronews.title: Bogs 'almost like a minefield': Europe's wetlands gain military importance
euronews.description: Peatlands are more than carbon sinks and havens for rare species. Amid rising security tensions, they are seen across Europe as natural barriers to attackers.

euronews.title: NASA astronaut films Southern Lights from SpaceX Dragon spacecraft
euronews.description: NASA astronaut Jessica Meir shared a stunning timelapse of the Southern Lights filmed from a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft. The aurora, triggered by recent solar activity, appears to dance across the atmosphere above Antarctica.

euronews.title: Ukraine: Strikes in Zaporizhzhia and Sumy kill three civilians and injure dozens
euronews.description: Ukraine reported fresh civilian casualties on 8 June after Russian drone strikes hit residential areas in Zaporizhzhia and Sumy.

euronews.title: Seven-time F1 world champion Lewis Hamilton facing backlash over anti-billionaire comments
euronews.description: A three-year-old interview with Lewis Hamilton has resurfaced online, which has prompted fresh conversation about society’s wealth gap, inequality, and for some, tone-deaf hypocrisy. Especially considering who his date was in Monaco last weekend...

euronews.title: ‘Putting biodiversity in our hands’: British wildlife will soon be celebrated on banknotes
euronews.description: Some say 'animal underdogs' have been left off the shortlist, which is now open to a public vote.

euronews.title: Watch: Inside the deepest diplomatic crisis between Poland and Ukraine
euronews.description: A recent military designation has sparked a major diplomatic crisis between Warsaw and Kyiv, exposing deeply conflicting national narratives. What has happened?

euronews.title: 'Heads must roll': France demands judicial overhaul after murder of 11-year-old girl
euronews.description: The main suspect, Jérôme Barella, had faced multiple complaints for sexual violence against minors but was never investigated or questioned - until now.

euronews.title: Books, authors and readers: a day at the Lisbon Book Fair
euronews.description: In Lisbon, June is about more than the popular saints’ festivities: it is also the month when Parque Eduardo VII turns into the country’s biggest bookshop. Ninety-six years after its first edition in 1930, the Book Fair still draws huge crowds. We went to find out why.

euronews.title: Around 20,000 people displaced by Philippine earthquake that killed at least 37
euronews.description: The Philippines is often hit by earthquakes and volcanic eruptions due to its location on the Pacific “Ring of Fire,” an arc of seismic faults around the ocean.

euronews.title: Newsletter: Squeezing Moscow's war chest
euronews.description: Also in this newsletter: A group of MEPs are up in arms over planned technical talks between EU and Taliban officials on the return of migrants to Afghanistan.

euronews.title: Where apartment prices are double those in Paris: Europe's most expensive housing markets
euronews.description: A new ranking shows Switzerland and Luxembourg dominate Europe's priciest property markets, with apartment prices in Zurich more than double those in Paris.

euronews.title: The EU’s migration pact takes full effect: are countries ready to deliver?
euronews.description: Co-legislators agreed on “return hubs” on 1 June, preparing to rollout the Migration and Asylum Pact of 12 June. Stricter border controls, uniform asylum rules, and a new digital monitoring system will crack down on illegal migration. But are member states ready for the new rules?

euronews.title: Europe Today: Former Italian PM Letta on Euronews as Iran halts attacks on Israel
euronews.description: Former Italian prime minister and President of the Jacques Delors Institute Enrico Letta speaks to Euronews. We also cover the Middle East, where Iran announced the end of military operations against Israel but warned of “a more crushing” response if it resumes strikes on Lebanon or its territory.

lemonde.title: Affaire Lyhanna : le gouvernement tente de canaliser la colère après le drame
lemonde.description: Sébastien Lecornu, qui tiendra une réunion interministérielle mardi, s’est engagé à amender le projet de loi sur la protection de l’enfance et à reprendre à son compte la proposition de loi intégrale visant à renforcer la lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes et aux enfants.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : la ville de Tyr, dans le sud du Liban, ciblée par l’armée israélienne, faisant au moins huit morts selon la défense civile libanaise
lemonde.description: Le porte-parole de l’armée israélienne, Avichay Adraee, a ordonné, mardi matin, l’évacuation de la ville libanaise, mentionnant que cela incluait le quartier chrétien et les camps et quartiers environnants.

lemonde.title: Finales NBA : Victor Wembanyama et les San Antonio Spurs contrarient New York, sous les yeux de Donald Trump hué par le public
lemonde.description: Après deux défaites à domicile, la franchise texane a remporté le troisième match des finales NBA, lundi à New York face aux Knicks (115-111). Présent dans les tribunes pour assister à cette rencontre, le président américain a été conspué par le Madison Square Garden.

lemonde.title: Drogues : un marché européen évoluant « à un rythme effréné » et aux substances « de plus en plus imprévisibles »
lemonde.description: Un rapport de l’Agence de l’Union européenne sur les drogues, publié mardi 9 juin, montre la mutation du trafic des stupéfiants et des habitudes des consommateurs, dans un contexte d’explosion de l’offre d’opioïdes de synthèse.

lemonde.title: Karim Bouamrane, maire PS de Saint-Ouen, se déclare candidat à l’élection présidentielle
lemonde.description: Interrogé sur France Inter, l’opposant interne à Olivier Faure a dit vouloir incarner « une France forte, humaine, qui protège, sécurise et donne la possibilité à chacune et chacun de pouvoir se soigner ».

lemonde.title: « Inviter un artiste dans un festival n’est pas l’ériger en ambassadeur culturel » : plus de 350 personnalités en soutien au cinéaste israélien Nadav Lapid
lemonde.description: Soumis à des pressions, le réalisateur, auteur du film « Oui », a renoncé à participer au FID Marseille. Dans une tribune au « Monde », un collectif de personnalités issues notamment du monde du cinéma s’inquiète de voir des logiques d’intimidation se substituer à la réflexion collective sur le rôle de la culture lors des crises politiques.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : dans la région de Kharkiv, les frappes russes nocturnes ont fait quatre morts, selon un nouveau bilan des autorités locales
lemonde.description: L’attaque aérienne russe, qui a eu lieu dans la nuit de lundi à mardi, a également fait une quinzaine de blessés dans cette région de l’est du pays.

lemonde.title: Affaire Patrick Bruel : la garde à vue du chanteur, visé par plusieurs plaintes pour violences sexuelles, prolongée de vingt-quatre heures
lemonde.description: L’artiste français de 67 ans est auditionné depuis lundi pour des faits concernant treize victimes, a fait savoir le parquet de Nanterre, qui centralise toutes les procédures le visant.

lemonde.title: JO 2030 : comment Nice a perdu les très rentables épreuves du « pôle glace » au profit de Lyon
lemonde.description: Alors que le choix de la ville azuréenne pour accueillir les sports de glace semblait acquis, le comité d’organisation a annoncé leur déménagement à Lyon. Un rebondissement de plus dans l’organisation de ces Jeux.

lemonde.title: « J’ai les yeux bridés, un nez écrasé, je suis petite. Quand on voit ma trisomie, on peut me parler comme à un enfant » : un concours d’éloquence pour surmonter son handicap
lemonde.description: Malgré la surdité, l’autisme ou la trisomie, six candidats se préparent à prononcer un discours en public, mardi 9 juin, au Théâtre Mogador, à Paris, pour la finale de Tous éloquents.

lemonde.title: Les grandes entreprises européennes alimentent les inégalités, selon Oxfam
lemonde.description: Dans un rapport traitant des cent plus grandes entreprises européennes en termes de chiffre d’affaires, l’ONG montre qu’elles reversent en moyenne 70 % de leurs bénéfices à leurs actionnaires et dénonce « un modèle qui ne profite qu’à une minorité ».

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Bruno Retailleau tente d’imposer son autorité aux « chapeaux à plumes » de la droite
lemonde.description: Candidat à la présidentielle pour Les Républicains depuis le vote des adhérents le 19 avril, le président du parti estime avoir la légitimité pour passer outre les réserves ou les critiques de certains ténors du parti, comme Jean-François Copé. Mais, à droite, l’autorité d’un chef n’est jamais tout à fait acquise.

lemonde.title: Au Pérou, Roberto Sanchez, candidat de gauche à l’élection présidentielle, devance d’un cheveu la conservatrice Keiko Fujimori après le dépouillement de 95 % des bulletins
lemonde.description: Pour qu’un vainqueur soit proclamé, des procès-verbaux contestés représentant quelque 450 000 votes seront examinés, ce qui pourrait prendre plusieurs jours.

lemonde.title: Agriculture : pourquoi les plus gros irrigants captent la majorité de l’eau dans les zones tendues
lemonde.description: Contrairement à d’autres pays, la France ne laisse pas la répartition de l’eau à la seule loi du marché, en confiant cette prérogative à des organismes locaux. Mais ce système est souvent critiqué pour son opacité et son déséquilibre à l’égard des nouveaux agriculteurs.

lemonde.title: En Argentine, la ville de Cutral Co mise sur une gigantesque statue de Lionel Messi pour attirer les touristes
lemonde.description: Dans cette cité de Patagonie, le capitaine de l’équipe nationale de football culminera à 26 mètres de haut. La municipalité, qui se cherche un avenir en dehors du pétrole, entend figurer au livre Guinness des records et faire venir du monde.

lemonde.title: Quel temps fait-il pour la saison ? Retrouvez « La Météo du Climat » du jour dans votre ville
lemonde.description: Consultez les prévisions météo dans votre ville ou votre région, associées à des données historiques mettant en lumière les écarts de température avec la moyenne des trente dernières années.

zeit.description: Kurz vor einem Treffen im Kanzleramt fordern die Spitzenverbände der Wirtschaft Reformzusagen von Schwarz-Rot. Auch wünschen sie sich einen »zeitlichen Fahrplan«.

zeit.description: Michael Vassiliadis, Chef der Gewerkschaft IGBCE, ist zu Gast beim Sozialgipfel des Kanzlers. Hier kritisiert er die Reformagenda und fordert einen Verteidigungssoli.

zeit.description: Entlang der Front haben russische Truppen ukrainisch kontrolliertes Gelände infiltriert. Bei Kupjansk sind sie an zwei Stellen vorgestoßen.

france24fr.title: Sahara occidental : trois membres du Front Polisario tués dont le fils d'un dirigeant historique
france24fr.description: Lehbib Mohamed Abdelaziz, haut responsable du Front Polisario et fils du dirigeant historique Mohamed Abdelaziz, a été tué dimanche 7 juin lors d'une frappe contre le mur des Sables, une immense structure fortifiée qui scinde le Sahara occidental sur une longueur de 2 700 km.

france24fr.title: Mozambique : Arlindo Chissale, l’activiste et journaliste qui en savait trop
france24fr.description: Le 7 janvier 2025, Arlindo Chissale, journaliste et activiste engagé en politique, disparaît sans laisser de trace dans la région du Cabo Delgado, en proie à une insurrection islamiste. Contact au Mozambique de la rédaction des Observateurs de France 24, il abordait de front les sujets les plus sensibles pour l'État mozambicain, au point de se mettre en danger, selon ses proches.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Fifa capitule et lâche l'arbitre somalien refoulé par les États-Unis
france24fr.description: L'arbitre somalien Omar Abdulkadir Artan, qui s'est vu refuser l'entrée sur le territoire américain samedi, n'officiera pas durant la Coupe du monde 2026, a annoncé la Fifa lundi dans un communiqué. L'instance internationale juge le pays hôte souverain en matière de visas accordés.

france24fr.title: "Opération Pouchkine" : sept Géorgiens jugés à Paris pour le vol de manuscrits russes originaux
france24fr.description: Sept personnes d'origine géorgiennes sont jugées à partir de mardi à Paris pour avoir dérobé des exemplaires originaux d’œuvres russes du XIXe siècle, notamment du célèbre poète et romancier Pouchkine, à Paris et Lyon. Plus largement, ils sont soupçonnées d'avoir participé à un réseau de voleurs d’ouvrages opérant au niveau européen.

france24fr.title: Kim Jong-un, "la transformation miraculeuse"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 9 juin, la visite, en ce moment, de Xi Jinping en Corée du nord. La première du dirigeant chinois depuis 2019. Les efforts de Donald Trump pour en finir avec la guerre avec l’Iran, alors que les Etats-Unis s’apprêtent à accueillir le Mondial, avec le Canade et les Etats-Unis. Et un triplé magnifique signé Michael Olise pour les Bleus, face à l'Irlande du Nord.

france24fr.title: Roman Abramovitch, l'oligarque russe adoubé par Zelensky pour amadouer Poutine
france24fr.description: Volodymyr Zelensky a assuré avoir demandé à l’homme d’affaires russe Roman Abramovitch de plaider auprès de Vladimir Poutine pour des négociations directes de paix. Le choix d’un oligarque resté fidèle au président russe peut surprendre, mais l'ex-patron de Chelsea tente depuis 2022 de jouer les médiateurs de guerre.

france24fr.title: L'équipe de France bat l'Irlande du Nord grâce à un triplé de Michael Olise
france24fr.description: Les Bleus se sont imposés (3-1) pour leur dernier match de préparation à la Coupe du monde. Michael Olise a inscrit un triplé, son premier chez les Bleus.

france24fr.title: Finale NBA : Trump hué pendant que Wembanyama relance les Spurs à New York
france24fr.description: Portés par Victor Wembanyama, auteur d'un match plein, les San Antonio Spurs se sont relancés avec un succès 115-111 lundi sur le parquet des New York Knicks, qui ne mènent plus que 2-1 en finale NBA. Juste avant le coup d'envoi du match, le président Donald Trump, présent, a été bruyamment hué par le public du Madison Square Garden.

france24fr.title: Le monde s'installe dans une nouvelle ère de violence élevée, selon une étude
france24fr.description: L'Institut de recherche sur la paix d'Oslo a dénombré 65 conflits impliquant au moins un État en 2025, du jamais vu depuis depuis 1946. Le nombre de conflits interétatiques a aussi doublé en un an pour passer à huit, là aussi un record en 80 ans.

france24fr.title: En direct : Israël appelle de nouveau à l'évacuation de tous les habitants de Tyr, au Liban
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne a appelé mardi les habitants de la ville de Tyr et de ses environs, dans le sud du Liban, à évacuer, en prévision de frappes contre le mouvement Hezbollah soutenu par l'Iran. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: IA : une semaine après Anthropic, OpenAI dépose son projet d'introduction en Bourse
france24fr.description: La société américain d'intelligence artificielle OpenAI a annoncé lundi avoir déposé de manière confidentielle son projet d'introduction en Bourse, une semaine après une annonce similaire de son rival Anthropic.

france24fr.title: Bruel : malgré la prescription, certaines accusations pourraient être jugées
france24fr.description: Ce lundi, Patrick Bruel, accusé de viols et d'agressions sexuelles par plusieurs femmes, a été placé en garde à vue. Il est auditionné, pour l'instant, sur des faits qui concernent treize victimes. Dans le même temps, on apprend que deux nouvelles plaintes pour viols ont été déposées contre lui. Une affaire qui fait resurgir la question de la prescription.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : attaque russe meurtrière à Kharkiv, Zelensky s'entretient avec les émissaires américains
france24fr.description: Volodymyr Zelensky a déclaré lundi avoir eu une discussion "très positive" avec les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, saluant leur disposition à relancer les négociations pour un règlement de la guerre en Ukraine. Sur le terrain, des frappes russes sur la région de Kharkiv, dans l'est de l'Ukraine, ont fait cinq morts et plusieurs blessés, ont annoncé tôt mardi les autorités locales.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : Israël et l'Iran suspendent leurs attaques à la demande de Trump
france24fr.description: Les combats entre Israël et Téhéran ont été suspendus lundi, après la reprise des hostilités la veille qui ont fait 15 blessés en Iran. Toutefois, chaque camp menace de reprendre les armes en cas d'attaque. Au Liban, 14 personnes ont péri dans des frappes israéliennes.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : les Bleus s'imposent contre l'Irlande du Nord pour leur dernier match préparatoire
france24fr.description: Michael Olise a offert lundi soir une victoire rassurante à l'équipe de France contre l'Irlande du Nord (3-1) en inscrivant un triplé lors de son dernier match de préparation du Mondial 2026 de football, quatre jours après une défaite surprise contre la Côte d'Ivoire.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : les compagnies aériennes affichent tarifs en hausse et bénéfices en baisse
france24fr.description: Le secteur aérien a un coup dans l'aile. Lors de sa réunion annuelle, l'IATA (Association du transport aérien international) annonce des marges revues à la baisse pour 2026, à 2% contre 4,2 % en 2025. Le bénéfice net anticipé est de seulement 23 milliards $ pour 2026, presque moitié moins que les 45 milliards $ de 2025, ce qui représente 4,50$ par passager transporté au lieu des 9,10 $ constatés l'année dernière. La guerre au Moyen-Orient ébranle tout le secteur, entre perturbations de l'espace

france24fr.title: Mesures sécuritaires au Mali: des zones d'intérêt militaires interdites aux civils
france24fr.description: Au Mali, face aux djihadistes qui mènent de plus en plus d'attaques vers le sud du pays, la junte malienne prend des décisions. L’une des dernières en date, l’instauration des zones d’intérêts militaires sur le territoire malien.

france24fr.title: "Fawn Mianju" : cette ingérence étrangère "made in China"
france24fr.description: Viginum, l'organisme français chargé de prévenir les ingérences numériques étrangères, a identifié un vaste réseau de propagande venu de Chine. Des pseudo-sites d'actualité et des comptes sur les réseaux sociaux visant à promouvoir la Chine, en lien direct avec la chaîne de télévision d'état chinoise CGTN.

nzz.description: Mit koordinierten Luftangriffen gegen Ziele in Iran haben Israel und die USA eine neue Phase der Eskalation im Nahen Osten eingeläutet. Die Gewalt bestimmt das Leben der Einwohner, von Teheran über Jerusalem bis nach Beirut. Die neuesten Entwicklungen in Bildern.

nzz.description: Die Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und der Hamas ist brüchig. Bis zu einem nachhaltigen Frieden im Nahen Osten ist es ein weiter Weg. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: «Es ist keine Überraschung, dass es wieder passiert ist», sagt der Sportkardiologe zur Herzattacke des Fussballers Christian Eriksen
nzz.description: Vor fünf Jahren brach Christian Eriksen zum ersten Mal bei einem Fussballspiel zusammen und musste wiederbelebt werden. Nun hatte er erneut eine Herzattacke auf dem Platz. Ein Kardiologe erklärt, wie das passieren konnte.

nzz.title: Ein Nazi-Tattoo, homophobe Sprüche und toxisches Verhalten gegenüber Frauen: Der linke Shootingstar Graham Platner wird für die Demokraten zur Hypothek

observador.title: O governo quer mesmo criar uma nova PIDE para os pobres?
observador.description: A juíza da Operação Marquês (que quer evitar duplicações), a nossa economia (que está num pântano) e os chocados da PSU (que só olham para um lado) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.description: O Luxemburgo somos "extraordinários", mas cá a ressaca é brava: faltam médicos e sobram processos. Com ministras a levar baile só o cavaquinho do ministro nos safa.

observador.title: Brasil. Partido de Lula tenta captar voto dos evangélicos
observador.description: "Continuamos a acreditar num Brasil onde a fé caminhe a par da justiça", afirma o partido. O eleitor evangélico, conservador e defensor da família tradicional representa 30% da população do país.

observador.title: Kim Jong-un diz que amizade com China é "tarefa estratégica"
observador.description: Na visita de Xi Jinping à Coreia do Norte, os líderes discutiram o reforço da cooperação, defesa da soberania, segurança e interesses, numa cimeira para fortalecer as relações bilaterais.

observador.title: Brookings vê China como principal beneficiária da guerra
observador.description: Pequim prefere manter relações com todos os países sem assumir responsabilidades sobre a segurança regional, defende o diretor do Centro. "Os EUA e Israel combateram o Irão e a China venceu".

observador.title: 8h. Ex-MAI diz que tinha falta de "conhecimentos técnicos"
observador.description: Em entrevista à Antena 1, a antiga governante diz ainda que sentiu "falta de autoridade" dentro do Executivo. Ainda, Papa Leão XIV visita hoje a cidade de Barcelona.

observador.title: Do Luxemburgo ao Japão: O estilo e a inteligência a reinar
observador.description: Mais um "desfile" da estilosa e original Margarida Maldonado Freitas que tem dado que falar. E ainda, o urso que anda perdido no Japão que ataca pessoas, mas que também bebe água da torneira.

observador.title: Eriksen quebra silêncio: «Desfibrilhador atuou bem»
observador.description: Eriksen garante que o desfibrilhador funcionou bem, enquanto Klopp ironiza sobre o seu futuro após as eleições do Real Madrid. No ciclismo, João Almeida volta a sofrer no Tour de Auvergne.

observador.title: Prejuízo do INEM aumentou para 7,6 milhões de euros em 2025
observador.description: Contas do instituto agravaram-se em 2025, devido ao aumento significativo das despesas com os parceiros do INEM, os bombeiros e a Cruz Vermelha. É o segundo ano consecutivo no vermelho.

observador.title: "Acordo que Trump quer vai comprar a próxima guerra"
observador.description: O coronel José do Carmo avisa que o desespero de Trump por um acordo isola Israel e fortalece o Irão. Admite ainda que este pacto não traz paz, está apenas a comprar a próxima guerra.

observador.description: Raman entrou na corrida eleitoral à última da hora, depois de ter apoiado Bass na sua candidatura à reeleição. Com a saída de Pratt da disputa, a batalha pela câmara transformou-se num duelo.

new-sci.title: You don't need to worry about recursive-self-improving AI – yet
new-sci.description: Anthropic has warned that recursive-self-improving AI could be on the horizon, but the truth is the company is more immediately concerned with marketing itself for a blockbuster initial public offering on the stock market, says Matthew Sparkes

new-sci.title: What really happened when ancient humans migrated out of Africa
new-sci.description: The out-of-Africa migration, in which ancient humans went on to inhabit every other continent except Antarctica, may not have been one moment in time, but a long and slow process. new-sci.title: What is a ‘normal’ memory slowdown, and when should I worry?
new-sci.description: Lapses in memory are a normal part of ageing but can also be signs of dementia. Here’s how to distinguish between typical brain ageing and cognitive decline

new-sci.title: Wildlife thrives in solar farm built on restored peatland
new-sci.description: A diverse range of bird species has been recorded at a solar park on rewetted peatland in Germany, suggesting that combining energy generation with habitat restoration could benefit biodiversity, the climate and the economy

new-sci.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer has warned tech firms, including Apple and Google, that they must voluntarily implement tools to stop children sharing explicit images, but experts warn this is easier said than done

new-sci.description: Each decade the world is losing over 7 per cent of its freshwater storage capacity to sediment build-up, according to an analysis of over half a million reservoirs

new-sci.title: Understanding anorexia’s grip on the brain could unlock new therapies
new-sci.description: One-third of people with anorexia nervosa don’t recover and treatment has remained stagnant for years. Now we’re beginning to understand how the condition takes over the mind

new-sci.title: Unpicking endometriosis reveals how it affects more than the pelvis
new-sci.description: Endometriosis is usually thought of as a gynaecological condition, but a huge study shows it has links with cholesterol levels, inflammation and an altered microbiome

new-sci.title: You could get some of the benefits of sleep without having to nod off
new-sci.description: Mice seemed to reap some of the benefits of sleep by having their brain activity stimulated while they were awake, and the researchers plan to test the approach on people

new-sci.title: Are we getting to the point where it's safe to gene-edit babies?

new-sci.title: The maths meme that has been distracting mathematicians for a century
new-sci.description: A seemingly simple set of rules kicks off a kind of mathematical magic trick, which has kept great minds busy since the 1930s. Columnist Jacob Aron explores the origins of the Collatz conjecture, why it is so addictive to mathematicians and whether AI could help us solve it once and for all

new-sci.title: Superintelligent machines may well need us after all
new-sci.description: Despite AI's dizzying improvements in mathematical ability, its successes show just how integral human mathematicians are to the scientific process

new-sci.title: Escher: The paradoxical artist beloved by mathematicians
new-sci.description: A new retrospective of M.C. Escher’s work opens this week. Explore some of his most mind-bending, mathematically inspired works here

new-sci.title: Cuts to US ocean programme will hinder monitoring of El Niño and AMOC
new-sci.description: Scientists warn that the Trump administration's push to dismantle a vital network of ocean-sensing instruments will stymie crucial weather and climate monitoring in the Pacific and Atlantic

new-sci.title: A chromosome from a frozen rat has been resurrected inside mice
new-sci.description: Mice that contain cells with an added rat chromosome have been created by scientists. The next step is to try this with frozen elephant tissue – and if that works, the team will try it with frozen mammoths

new-sci.title: Alice Roberts: 'We are fundamentally, at the end of the day, animals'
new-sci.description: Why do we have big brains? Or walk on two legs? Biological anthropologist and broadcaster Alice Roberts talks human exceptionalism, evolution and her new book Humans with Michael Marshall

new-sci.title: Mysterious ‘cold blob’ in the Atlantic suggests the AMOC is weakening
new-sci.description: A patch of ocean south-east of Greenland is the only place on Earth that is cooling, and it could be a sign that the warm water "conveyor belt" in the Atlantic is slowing down

new-sci.title: Why you need to future-proof your brain in middle age and how to start
new-sci.description: Ages 40 to 65 see a period of turmoil in the brain that has previously been overlooked. But identifying problems during this time can protect your cognitive health for decades to come

phys-org.title: Hundreds evacuated as waves batter New Zealand capital
phys-org.description: Authorities evacuated hundreds of people from their seaside homes in New Zealand's capital Tuesday as 11-meter (36-foot) waves lashed the coast.

phys-org.title: Number of conflicts between states reaches highest level since World War II
phys-org.description: The number of conflicts between states continued to increase sharply in 2025 and has now reached the highest level since World War II. At the same time, the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP) at Uppsala University registered a record total number of armed conflicts.

phys-org.title: Koala population crash came before humans, genomic study reveals
phys-org.description: A genomic study has reshaped our understanding of the evolutionary history of the koala (Phascolarctos cinereus), revealing the iconic Australian marsupial experienced a severe population decline around 100,000 years ago, before the arrival of humans on the continent.

phys-org.title: More people with disabilities are seeking work, report reveals
phys-org.description: The June 2026 National Trends in Disability Employment (nTIDE) report reveals a large increase in job-seeking among people with disabilities, signaling that more individuals are entering the labor force as economic pressure intensifies. This finding aligns with last month's nTIDE forecast that rising prices would push more people with disabilities to seek employment, while progress in employment access continues.

phys-org.title: MLB swing-tracking data helps researchers examine baseball's long-debated two-strike approach
phys-org.description: When baseball fans watch a batter strike out with runners in scoring position, the reaction is often immediate: Shorten the swing. Put the ball in play. Stop swinging for the fences, they lament.

phys-org.title: Expedition to Antarctica advances research on potential melanoma treatment
phys-org.description: Deep beneath the icy waters surrounding Antarctica, a small marine organism may hold clues to a future cancer treatment. Researchers from USF recently returned from a six-week expedition in one of the most remote environments on Earth to study a species of ascidian, or sea squirt, that contains a bacterium capable of killing melanoma cancer cells.

phys-org.title: Finding hidden catalytic knowledge from literature data
phys-org.description: Exciting new research at Tohoku University's Advanced Institute for Materials Research (WPI-AIMR) explains how to transform decades of scattered literature data into computable design rules for catalysts. By using human intelligence, regression models, and AI agents, researchers can accelerate the discovery of efficient, low-cost catalysts for clean energy technologies like fuel cells, water splitting, and CO₂ reduction. phys-org.title: Politicization in humanities scholarship may compromise scholarly standards
phys-org.description: A national report co-authored by a University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa sociologist has found that while the humanities and social sciences continue to produce rigorous and valuable scholarship, some disciplines are experiencing instances where scholarly standards have been compromised as political considerations shape research and academic evaluation.

phys-org.title: Protected bike lanes, not painted lanes, lift NYC bikeshare ridership, analysis shows
phys-org.description: Protected bike lanes increase Citi Bike ridership in New York City, but painted bike lanes and sharrows do not show a statistically significant causal effect on ridership after accounting for confounding factors, according to a new study from researchers at NYU's Tandon School of Engineering published this week in npj Sustainable Mobility and Transport.

phys-org.title: 50 years of data reveals true extent of climate change impacts on kelp forests
phys-org.description: New research from the University of Victoria (UVic) has found that some kelp forests around Vancouver Island were disappearing far earlier than scientists previously thought, highlighting that climate change has been altering ecosystems long before most people were aware anything was wrong.

phys-org.title: Artemis II moon mission research continues on Earth
phys-org.description: Since NASA's Artemis II crew members safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10 after their record-setting mission around the moon, science teams have been busy collecting more data and combing through observations collected on the test flight. Results from these science investigations will help support safe human exploration of deep space and provide a blueprint for how future missions will conduct science on the lunar surface as NASA builds a moon base and develops an enduring

phys-org.title: NASA's INCUS mission on road to launch, study storms from space
phys-org.description: Teams working on NASA's INCUS (Investigation of Convective Updrafts) mission, the first space-based survey of the dynamics of tropical convective storms, have completed assembly and tested two of the mission's small satellites, or SmallSats. Testing continues on the third SmallSat and is scheduled for completion no earlier than September ahead of a 2027 launch.

phys-org.title: Agricultural waste can be used to clean wastewater
phys-org.description: Water pollution caused by pharmaceuticals, pesticides and other organic contaminants is an increasing global issue, especially in regions with limited wastewater treatment infrastructure. A new doctoral thesis from Umea University in Sweden offers an innovative and sustainable solution by demonstrating how agricultural waste can be converted into effective materials for water purification.

phys-org.title: They call it 'stupid hot' for a reason: Heat muddles animal brains
phys-org.description: On a blazing hot day in South Africa, female southern pied babblers can't think straight. The medium-sized black-and-white birds are trying to get at tasty mealworms behind a see-through barrier. On cooler days, the birds can quickly figure out that all they have to do is go around the small wall of plastic. But when the mercury goes up, the birds just keep stubbornly pecking at the barrier.

phys-org.title: Cosmic bombardment may have opened Earth's crust for prebiotic chemistry
phys-org.description: Asteroids and planetesimals regularly bombarded Earth between about 4.6 billion and 3.5 billion years ago, during the Hadean and Archean eons. Because few rocks today are more than 4 billion years old, our understanding of the planet's environment during that time is limited. However, samples from the moon and its cratered surface hint at the period's rate of cosmic impacts.

phys-org.title: Super sponge can remove toxic dyes from industrial wastewater
phys-org.description: Colors brighten our lives and help define countless items we use daily—from the vibrant clothes we wear to decorative paper and packaging materials. What adds different colors to these things? Dyes, which bind themselves to the structure of the material they are coloring. For example, methylene blue (MB) is a dye used to color paper, leather products, silk and wool, and is also employed as a diagnostic agent and in the rubber and cosmetic industries. But what happens after these dyes have served

phys-org.title: How plants survive constant DNA damage: Newly identified repair protein protects growth-critical stem cells
phys-org.description: Similar to the way DNA damage can contribute to human diseases such as cancer, it can also disrupt growth, development and survival in plants. Every day, plants endure environmental stresses such as sunlight, radiation, drought and soil stress—all of which can damage their DNA. However, they cannot move away from danger. How do plants handle all that damage?

phys-org.title: Despite toxic reputation, our research shows podcasts can help men's mental health
phys-org.description: Over the last decade, podcasts have become big business, with more than a fifth of UK adults listening to podcasts each week. The format particularly resonates with men, who are more likely than women to identify as podcast fans. Men are also overrepresented as podcast hosts.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.
